newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dlr vols easier as spot slips in Europe.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr vols easier as spot slips in Europe.

text.p: Dollar volatilities eased in Europe, tracking spot's stumble below 1.73 mark and 116 yen, but they remained bid on dips as debate over the strength and timing of Europe's single currency rumbled on.
"Volatilities are a bit softer in Europe, as spot declines," said Michel Jean-Baptiste, head of global options trading at Banque Indosuez in Paris.

Dollar/mark one-month implied volatilities drifted to 9.80/10.20 percent at 1200 GMT in Europe against 10.15/35 earlier and 10.30/60 in late Europe on Monday. Options traders said the slide followed on the heels of weaker spot dollar.
Dollar/yen one-month vols were also a touch softer but off early lows and at midday in Europe stood at 10.70/11.00 percent, after spot dollar/yen hovered below 116 yen in Europe.

Spot dollar, boosted in Europe after a buying spree inspired by EMU uncertainty in the wake of France's turn left in weekend parliamentary elections, was off highs in Europe as it dipped below 1.73 marks and 116 yen.
At 1220 GMT dollar/mark was trading at 1.7257/64 against 1.7265/75 in late Europe and 115.88/98 yen against 116.55/65.
With EMU uncertainty dominating European trade, analysts said the dollar and dollar vols would remain bid on dips.
"What is clear is that volatilities will rise again as EMU is still unresolved," said an options trader at a US bank.
Dollar/yen one-month vols edge off early lows, standing at 10.70/11.00 percent at 1235 GMT, though steady against 10.40/70 in late Europe on Monday.

Mark/French franc one-month implied vols ease further, standing at 1.50/2.00 percent from 2.20/50 percent earlier as spot mark skids lower against its European crosses amid expectations the government will compromise with the Bundesbank over revaluing its assets.
